items.title: Hezbollah vows retaliation as Israeli strikes devastate Lebanon

items.description: Hezbollah condemned what it called Israel's "barbaric aggression" on Wednesday and declared it has the "natural and legal right to resist occupation and respond to its attacks," after Israeli warplanes carried out the deadliest wave of strikes on Lebanon since the current conflict began in March. items.title: Russian warship escorts sanctioned tankers through English Channel

featured_image.name: Exclusive: Putin mocks Starmer with warship in Channel - Yahoo

items.description:
A Russian naval frigate escorted two sanctioned oil tankers through the English Channel on Wednesday, in what observers described as a direct challenge to Prime Minister Keir Starmer's threat to seize vessels belonging to Moscow's shadow fleet. The Admiral Grigorovich, a guided-missile frigate armed with anti-ship, cruise, and surface-to-air missiles, sailed between the two tankers as they passed the south coast of England, according to The Telegraph, which reported observing the convoy from a vessel off Dover.[1][2][3]

A British Royal Fleet Auxiliary vessel trailed the Russian formation but made no attempt to board or intercept the sanctioned ships. One of the tankers was identified as the Universal.[3][4][1]

items.title: Vance questions Iranian speaker's English as ceasefire rift grows

featured_image.name: Vance says Iran faces 'two pathways' as deadline nears in ...

items.description:
U.S. Vice President JD Vance on Wednesday dismissed Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf's claims that Washington had violated the newly declared ceasefire, questioning whether the senior Iranian official could properly "understand English" and casting the dispute as evidence that the two sides are closer to agreement than Tehran admits.

Vance's combative remarks came hours after Ghalibaf alleged that three of the 10 points in Iran's proposed negotiating framework had already been breached before formal talks could begin — citing Israel's continued strikes on Lebanon, a drone allegedly entering Iranian airspace, and Washington's refusal to recognize Iran's right to enrich uranium.[1][2][3]

items.title: Trump weighs relocating troops to punish NATO allies over Iran war

featured_image.name: Trump suggests in new interviews he is 'absolutely' considering withdrawing  US from 'paper tiger' NATO | CNN

items.description:
The Trump administration is considering a plan to relocate U.S. troops away from NATO member countries it views as uncooperative during the Iran war and reposition them in nations that showed greater support for the military campaign, The Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday, citing administration officials.[1][2]

The proposal, which has circulated among senior officials in recent weeks and gained backing, remains in its early stages. It is one of several punitive options the White House is discussing to penalize NATO members that declined to assist during the U.S.-Israeli bombing campaign, which began in late February.[2]

items.title: Artemis II crew to hold press conference from deep space tonight

featured_image.name: WATCH: NASA holds daily Artemis II news conference after releasing ...

items.description:
Four astronauts aboard NASA's Orion spacecraft are coasting back toward Earth on Wednesday after completing a record-breaking lunar flyby, with the crew scheduled to hold their first in-space press conference later tonight as they near the end of a 10-day voyage around the moon.

The 20-minute virtual news conference is set for 9:45 p.m. EDT on Wednesday, April 8, with NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, and Christina Koch, along with Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen, answering media questions from roughly 200,000 miles away.[1]

items.title: UAE demands Iran pay reparations after 40 days of attacks

featured_image.name: UAE has an active role in Iran war and will be pounded if US ...

items.description:
The United Arab Emirates on Wednesday demanded that Iran be held "accountable and fully liable for damages and reparations" following weeks of devastating aerial attacks, as Abu Dhabi sought clarity on the terms of a fragile two-week ceasefire announced by President Donald Trump.

In an official statement, the UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs said the "unprovoked Iranian attacks targeting infrastructure, energy facilities, and civilian sites over the past 40 days — which included 2,819 ballistic and cruise missiles, as well as drones — and the resulting loss of life and property damage, necessitate a firm position". The ministry said it was seeking clarification from Washington on the ceasefire's provisions to ensure "Iran's full commitment to an immediate cessation of all hostilities in the region and the complete and unconditional reopening of the Strait of Hormuz".[1]

items.title: Iran recloses Strait of Hormuz, threatening U.S. ceasefire

featured_image.name: Iran's parliament backs blocking Strait of Hormuz

items.description:
Iran shut down the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday, less than 24 hours after agreeing to a two-week ceasefire with the United States, casting immediate doubt over whether the fragile truce that ended more than five weeks of war could survive. Tehran cited Israel's continued strikes on Lebanon as a violation of the agreement, while Washington called the closure "completely unacceptable."[1][2]

The ceasefire, brokered with Pakistan's help and announced Tuesday evening just hours before a deadline set by President Donald Trump, had hinged on what the U.S. described as the "complete, immediate, and safe opening" of the strait — a waterway responsible for roughly a fifth of the world's oil supply. Iran confirmed it would allow passage "in coordination with Iranian armed forces," but Israeli strikes on Beirut that killed more than 100 people overnight appeared to upend that commitment.[3][4][5]
